Nature accepts a compiled PDF from standard LaTeX at initial submission and imposes house style after acceptance; this is a review-friendly proxy, not a reproduction of Nature's proprietary layout.
name: Nature Machine Intelligence (Article)
review: single-anonymized by default; double-anonymized is optional and author-selected

limits.note: Article profile verified from the live NMI content-type and submission pages on 2026-08-11; main-text words exclude abstract, Methods, references, and figure legends

notes: Article: up to 3,500 main-text words, excluding abstract, Methods, references and figure legends; abstract up to 150 unreferenced words; up to six main display items; typically up to 50 references
official Article order: unheaded Introduction, Results, Discussion, Methods; Results and Methods use topical subheadings, while Discussion has none
initial submission is format-flexible and accepts a compiled PDF from TeX/LaTeX; the generated standard-article proxy is for authoring and review, not Nature house style
production artwork: original research uses 88mm and 180mm figure widths, RGB colour, editable vector art where possible, and 5–7pt sans-serif labels; the scaffold uses the upper 7pt bound
up to ten Extended Data display items; put Editio-managed Extended Data in a section classed deo:SupplementaryInformationDescription so the doctor can count it separately
double-anonymized review is optional; authors are responsible for anonymization, and author details move to the cover letter

after acceptance in principle, Nature requires editable Word or standard LaTeX source, numerical references embedded in the manuscript, and no personal macros; final packaging is a later editio-venue concern
